answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it earns influence, then randomly sample identities for costly tasks and slash bonds when independently verified answers conflict with the task’s ground truth. A sybil attacker must split capital across many bonds, risking each one, rather than minting free accounts; the stake also has an opportunity cost while locked. The shale, glacier, and opal markets may differ, but the same rule makes fake identities expensive without pretending it proves personhood.
